newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end at record high on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end at record high on late buying.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed at a record high for the second consecutive day on Thursday, following a late spurt of foreign-led buying in blue-chips, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index ended 5.34 points, or 0.73 percent, at a day high of 735.49 points after touching a day low of 729.56 points earlier. Advancers led decliners by 76 to 42 with 71 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 503 billion rupiah.
The index recorded its previous closing high of 734.02 points on Wednesday.

"It's a surprise closing after the index moved in a very narrow range most of the day. The rise at the close was mostly due to active buying in Telkom," one sales manager with a large state-owned brokerage firm said.
The sales manager said Indonesia's strong economic fundamentals coupled with agressive local investors were likely to keep pushing the index up in the near-term.

Blue-chip Telkom, the heaviest weighted stock on the index, rose 100 rupiah to 4,150 with about three million shares traded, while Indosat gained 150 rupiah to 7,625 rupiah with some 777,000 shares changing hands.
"Foreign fund managers are targetting Indonesia's liquid blue-chips including Telkom and Indosat as they are considered to benefit a lot from the country's strong economic showings," one broker said.
Indonesia's latest macroeconomic figures indicate its economy is buoyant and inflation is under control but slow growth in non-oil exports is slightly worrying, economists said on Thursday.

The government announced on Wednesday that the consumer price index fell 0.17 percent month-on-month in June, after a 0.19 percent rise in May, while annual inflation slipped to 4.98 percent from 5.08 percent.

It said also that the trade surplus of the country, the only Asian member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries, rose to $540.3 million from $243.3 million in March and $366.2 million in April 1996.
Agressive local buying in second-liners also helped boost the index at the close, brokers said.
